plot: On Halloween morning Max wears Grandma's floppy dog ears and Dog wears little cat ears, and they bet a pumpkin cookie that Grandma won't spot the swap; Max has to fetch, roll and bark (a 'mee-woof'), Dog eats Max's fish and purrs like a fridge, until the tired pair decide to tell the truth together and find out Grandma knew since breakfast from Max's question-mark tail and Dog's wag, then she shows her own costume, big mouse ears, and splits the cookie; next morning the big pumpkin has one tiny bite in it.

script.title: Max Turned Into a Dog for Halloween

beats.say: Meow! Cats climb sofas, right? Up I go! Whoaaa!
Shh, Dog! Grandma will hear! Woof! I mean... woof!
Can a cat and a dog swap places for a whole day?
It's Halloween morning. Max had the silliest idea ever.
Max wears Grandma's floppy brown dog ears.
And Dog wears pointy cat ears. Very tiny on his big head.
Today I'm Dog, and you're Max. Grandma will never know!
I am Max. I am a cat. I do cat things. Meow.
I'm the judge. Whoever Grandma spots first loses.
Easy. I'm the best dog ever. Look at my floppy ears!
The winner gets Grandma's first pumpkin cookie.
Cookie! I mean... meow. A cookie. How nice. Meow.
Grandma comes in with breakfast. Everybody freezes.
Good morning, my two Halloween pumpkins!
Grandma smiles a little smile. And winks at Mouse.
Max sits very still. His tail curls up like a question mark.
And Dog's tail? Wag, wag, wag. It never stops.
Dog, dear. Time to play. Fetch your red ball!
Fetch? Me? Oh. Yes. Woof! Fetching!
Max chases the ball across the rug. It bounces off his nose.
Got it! In my mouth! Bleh. It tastes like old socks.
Hey! That's my favorite taste! I mean... meow.
Good boy! Now roll over, Dog! Roll, roll, roll!
Max rolls once. Twice. Three times. The whole room spins.
Is the sofa upside down? Or is it me?
And now, Max, dear. Your fish snack is ready.
Dog looks at the fish. Dog has never eaten fish.
Crunch, munch. Hey! Fish is GREAT! Meow, meow!
That's my fish! Being a dog is not fair!
Careful! Grandma is looking very closely now.
One wrong move, and you lose the pumpkin cookie!
Max, dear, come sit on my lap and purr for me.
Purr? Uh-oh. I don't know how to purr.
Dog climbs on Grandma's lap. Very slowly. He is very big.
Mmmmmmmmm. Brrrrrrrr. Mmmmmmmm.
My, my. That's a very deep purr today.
And Max, dear, you feel a little... bigger today.
It's my fluffy morning fur. Very fluffy. Meow.
He sounds like the fridge! I can't stop laughing!
Max! Dogs don't giggle like that. Act like a dog!
Then the doorbell rings. Ding dong!
Dog, dear, who's at the door? Go and bark!
Bark? I have to bark? Real dogs bark so loud.
Max runs to the door. He takes a big breath.
Mee-WOOF! Mee-woof, mee-woof!
A meow-woof?! That's not a bark! She'll know for sure!
It's only the mail. A little card falls through the door.
It says Happy Halloween, from Luna! She'd love this game.
Mouse is right. One more mistake, and we're caught!
Max, I mean, Dog. Max? I forgot who I am.
Being someone else is hard work. Max is tired.
Fetching is hard. Barking is hard. And Dog got my fish.
Purring is hard. Climbing is harder. My ears are too small.
Okay. Let's tell Grandma the truth. Together.
Even if we lose the pumpkin cookie?
Even if we lose the cookie. No more tricks.
They walk to Grandma, slowly, side by side.
Grandma, we have to tell you something big.
Do you mean that you're Max, dear? And he is Dog?
You knew? Since when?
Since breakfast. Your tail curled like a question mark.
Max's tail always does that. And cats don't wag, Dog.
My tail told on me! Bad tail. Good tail. Happy tail!
So why did you play along all morning?
Because it's Halloween. And because I have a costume too!
Grandma puts on two big, round, grey ears.
Grandma is a mouse! Grandma is ME!
So who wins the pumpkin cookie?
You both told the truth together. So you both win.
Grandma breaks the cookie in two. One half for each.
Being Dog was fun for one morning. But being me is best.
Me too. But can I keep the fish?
That night, the big pumpkin sits by the door.
In the morning, it has one tiny bite in it. Who?
A bite in Grandma's pumpkin? I'm going to find out!
